name: cert-manager
tagline: TLS certificates, issued and renewed inside the cluster
description: When every certificate expires, which renewals are stuck and exactly where — the request, the ACME order or the challenge — and why, in plain words. Panels on certificates, issuers, Ingresses and Gateways.
author: K8s Dockside

name: OpenBao & Vault
tagline: seal state, HA leaders, and which workloads get which secrets
description: A padlock per server cluster, open or shut, with the unseal keys as slots and the leader and standbys as a small picture, and what needs a person worst first: a sealed node, no leader, a failing sync, a certificate about to expire. A secret flow from the server through the Vault Secrets Operator, External Secrets, CSI or the agent injector to the Kubernetes Secret and the workloads using it, and PKI certificates and leases on a timeline. Tells OpenBao and HashiCorp Vault apart on its own, and never reads a Secret, a key or a token. Panels on server pods, every other pod and the Secrets Operator's objects.
author: K8s Dockside

name: Longhorn
tagline: distributed block storage: volumes, replicas and the disks under them
description: Longhorn's own dashboard, in the app: volume health, node and disk status as three rings, and one bar for how much room is left. A volume map with a pill per replica in the mode the engine has it in and a live bar for anything rebuilding, nodes with every disk's capacity and what is promised on it, and a data protection page that says which volumes have no backup at all. Panels on PersistentVolumeClaims, Nodes and Longhorn Volumes.
author: K8s Dockside

name: Rook Ceph
tagline: Ceph in Kubernetes: health, capacity, pools and every storage class
description: Ceph's own health checks written out in full, the raw capacity as one bar, and every mon, manager and OSD by the machine it runs on. A storage class map that groups every Ceph class by what it hands a workload — block, shared file, NFS, S3 bucket — and ties each to the pool, filesystem or object store behind it, with the redundancy of that pool: one keeping a single copy is called out even while Ceph reports HEALTH_OK. Works on a cluster that runs Ceph, on one that only consumes an external Ceph, and on a pure CSI client with no operator at all. Panels on PersistentVolumeClaims, StorageClasses, Nodes and CephClusters.
author: K8s Dockside

name: CloudNativePG
tagline: PostgreSQL in Kubernetes: clusters, replication, backups and poolers
description: A card per Postgres cluster with its state in words, its primary and standbys as a small picture, how old its last backup is against its own schedule and how far back a restore can reach. A topology of each cluster with the node and zone every instance runs on and the poolers and services in front, and every backup on a timeline with each failure's error in full. Back up now, hibernate, wake up and restart, each shown before it is made. Panels on Clusters, their pods and their volumes.
author: K8s Dockside

name: MetalLB
tagline: load balancer addresses for bare-metal clusters
description: Every address pool as a map of its addresses, the route each address takes out of the cluster, and what is wrong with it. Services still waiting for an address come first, with the reason and a fix.
author: K8s Dockside

name: Envoy Gateway
tagline: Gateway API traffic through Envoy, from listener to backend
description: Every Gateway with its addresses, listeners and proxies, a traffic map from listener to route to the Service behind it that shows where the path breaks, and every policy with what it is attached to and what it does in plain words. Panels on Gateways, routes and policies.
author: K8s Dockside

name: Gateway API
tagline: where your traffic goes: Gateways, listeners, routes and backends, drawn as a map
description: A traffic map from Gateway to listener to route to the Service behind it, with canary weights on the edges and a dashed red edge wherever the path breaks: a refused route, a missing Service, a namespace crossed without a ReferenceGrant. Type an address and see which listener and rule it lands on, what the filters do to it and where it ends up, by the Gateway API's own matching rules. Works with any implementation and only reads. Panels on Gateways, routes and Services.
author: K8s Dockside

name: Cilium
tagline: eBPF networking, identities and the policies between them
description: Every endpoint as a hexagon coloured by whether policy protects it, every network policy drawn as a flow from who may connect to where it may go, the datapath read from cilium-config, and nodes, LB IPAM pools, L2 announcements and BGP sessions with what is wrong with them.
author: K8s Dockside

name: Calico
tagline: pod networking, IPAM and tiered network policy
description: Policy tiers as lanes in the order Calico evaluates them, a trace of one pod's traffic tier by tier, every IP pool as a map of its blocks and addresses, the BGP mesh and peers with their session states, and Whisker's flow logs: who talks to whom and what is denied, by which policy.
author: K8s Dockside

name: Kube-OVN
tagline: VPCs, subnets and IPAM on OVN
description: Every subnet with what it has handed out against what it has left, and the addresses in it by the pod holding each one. VPC topology draws each logical router with the subnets hanging off it. The overview checks ovs-ovn and kube-ovn-cni on every node, because Kube-OVN's control plane stays green while its dataplane is down.
author: K8s Dockside

name: Flannel
tagline: one subnet per node, joined by an overlay
description: The cluster network drawn to scale with every node's lease placed where it actually falls, and the backend that joins them with the endpoint and VTEP MAC each node is reached at. Names the nodes holding no lease, leases falling outside the network, and nodes whose backend disagrees with net-conf.json.
author: K8s Dockside

name: KubeVirt
description: Your fleet of virtual machines at a glance, the nodes hosting them and the migrations in flight, with Start, Pause, Restart, Migrate and Stop on every machine and guest charts from Prometheus.
author: K8s Dockside

name: Image inventory
description: Every image in the cluster by registry, the workloads using it, and the risky ones — unpinned tags and images that will not pull. Works on any cluster. Also the starting point for writing a plugin of your own in TypeScript.
author: K8s Dockside

name: Optimization advisor
tagline: a score for this cluster, and what to change to raise it
description: Checks requests and limits, replicas and disruption budgets, probes, autoscalers, idle volumes and node headroom against plain rules, scores the cluster, and says what to change. Switch rules off, accept findings, and rightsize from Prometheus, VictoriaMetrics or metrics-server. Works on any cluster.
author: K8s Dockside

name: Descheduler
tagline: evicts pods that should be running somewhere else
description: Whether anything is rebalancing this cluster, and what it moved. Every eviction the descheduler recorded, live, with the plugin that asked for it and the node the pod left — refusals beside the successes, because an eviction a PodDisruptionBudget turned down is the one worth reading. Its policy as forms rather than YAML: every plugin with a sentence on what it does, thresholds and limits as fields, checked against what the descheduler refuses at startup, and the file shown before it is applied. Panels on Pods saying whether this pod could be evicted at all, and on Nodes for what has left them.
author: K8s Dockside

name: Vitistack
tagline: a supervisor cluster -- networks, clusters, machines and their VMs -- as one picture
description: Every network namespace, Kubernetes cluster, machine provider, machine and VM as one node graph that lights up the chains through whatever you select, with what is failing and why. Cluster and machine pages in full, and every cluster against the Kubernetes release calendar and the Talos support matrix, with buttons that start talos-operator's upgrades.
author: K8s Dockside

name: GPU & Accelerators
tagline: GPUs and other devices, through device plugins or DRA
description: Every accelerator counted once, whether a device plugin or a DRA driver advertises it: how many are in use, how many are free and what pending pods are waiting for, by model and vendor, with the reasons in words. An inventory with a square per device on its node, coloured free, in use, shared or unhealthy, MIG instances drawn across it, and the pods using each. Panels on Nodes, Pods and ResourceClaims, and DCGM charts when there is a Prometheus.
author: K8s Dockside
